summary: Marketing is advancing on multiple fronts, with the China Going-Global report and Tech in Asia event as immediate priorities, while SEO focus sharpens on Asia Star and Intelligent China, and the knowledge website redesign moves toward an editorial style.
summaryDetail: The most urgent work this week centers on the China Going-Global report and the Tech in Asia (TIA) event on Sep 15-16. For the report, finalize copy changes ('Led by' instead of 'chaired by') and prepare the digital version and printed one-page flyer for TIA, with Ira reviewing the flyer copy. For TIA, launch the Luma page, remove Dean Xiang's speech from the agenda, and confirm Melvin's availability for a call with Tech in Asia. Meanwhile, SEO prioritization is set: Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top programs, with Joseph drafting target areas and prompts, and the team analyzing existing participants and CRM leads to refine targeting. The knowledge website redesign is progressing with an editorial-style approach—more articles on the homepage, centered menu, and indices like BCI/BSI featured—with feedback due from Joseph, Julie, and the team lead, and Joker to adjust the design. Additionally, there's an operational issue: Outlook accounts are locked due to old passwords, requiring all team members to delete and re-login on all devices and contact JSB for backend unlock. Longer-term, Global Foundation membership renewal and collaboration calls are on the horizon, and the AACSB Global Impact Awards 2027 application is being considered.
